figure_dir <- params$figure_dir

## Source and measurement

The saved City-traffic-M data describe 720 supplied road segments in Yekaterinburg on 2024-10-18. They originate from version 4 of `mightyneghbor/city-traffic-benchmarks`, with volume and static-feature Parquet sources. The bundled records are from `city_traffic_M_osm_congestion_sample.json`.

Each fifteen-minute frame is the saved mean of three five-minute observations. The payload does not establish the physical volume unit; values retain the label `source volume`. Speed is retained as `source speed` without conversion.

The saved congestion index combines slowdown relative to each segment's 90th-percentile speed with a clipped log-volume weight. The report uses that existing index and its supplied display scale. It is a derived indicator, not an official congestion label.

## Data preparation

`prepare.R` aligns the supplied segment IDs, coordinates and saved frames. It preserves the volume, speed and congestion arrays and their source summaries, then writes `data/input.rds`. It performs no further temporal averaging or segment selection.

```{r prepare}
library(bdynets)
source("prepare.R")
prepared_file <- prepare_example(".")
x <- read_traffic(prepared_file)
input <- readRDS(prepared_file)
x$basemap <- traffic_basemap(x,cache_dir=file.path("data","basemap-cache"))
x$provenance$basemap <- x$basemap$provenance
runtime_context <- x$basemap
index <- match(params$time_label,sub("^.* ","",x$time_labels))
stopifnot(!is.na(index))
```

The map starts at `r x$time_labels[index]` and covers
`r x$interval_seconds[index]/60` minutes. The default 08:00 is a demonstration
selection, not a maximum-based selection. Numeric seconds and displayed labels
retain the supplied source clock; they do not establish a UTC offset.

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Item=c("Roads","Frames","First interval start","Last interval start","Flow unit"),
  Value=c(nrow(x$roads),length(x$times),x$time_labels[1],tail(x$time_labels,1),x$unit)),
  caption="Data scope")
```

| Common field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| road_id | Unique directed road or segment identifier |
| geometry | Longitude/latitude vertex matrix, ordered in travel direction |
| time | Source-clock interval start in numeric seconds |
| flow | Supplied nonnegative measurement; zero is observed and NA is missing |
| unit | Supplied measurement label, without inferred conversion |

```{r sample-records}
knitr::kable(head(input$flow),caption="Actual prepared flow records")
```

## Whole-day coverage

```{r day-coverage}
coverage <- traffic_coverage(x)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic=c("Expected road-time cells","Observed cells","Missing cells","Observed zero cells"),
  Value=unlist(coverage[c("road_time_cells","observed","missing","zero")],use.names=FALSE)),
  caption="All supplied roads and intervals")
```

A road-time cell is one road in one interval. These counts cover the whole day,
including roads outside the central-area map view. An omitted pair and an explicit
NA are missing; neither is replaced by zero.

## Selected-time map and statistics

```{r map, fig.cap="Saved source-volume observations at the selected fifteen-minute interval. The map focuses on the central spatial range; all 720 supplied segments enter the statistics."}
plot(x,index=index)
```

The common log1p algorithm uses all supplied values to establish the day's
thresholds. Red means higher source volume, not a verified congested state.
Speed-limit and maximum-volume attributes do not choose a plotting style.

```{r selected-statistics}
selected <- traffic_summary(x,index=index)
knitr::kable(selected[c("time","roads","available","missing","zero")],
  caption="Selected-interval availability")
knitr::kable(selected[c("minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=2,caption=paste("Selected-interval distribution [",x$unit,"]"))
```

At `r selected$time`, mean source volume is `r fmt(selected$mean)` and the
median is `r fmt(selected$median)`. There are `r fmt(selected$zero,0)` observed
zero values and `r fmt(selected$missing,0)` missing values in this interval.

## Daily pattern and limits

```{r daily-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Saved meanVolume series from the source frames. The dashed line marks the selected map time."}
trend <- traffic_trend(x,method="provided")
plot(trend,metric="mean",index=index)
peak <- which.max(trend$mean)
```

The greatest saved meanVolume is `r fmt(trend$mean[peak])` at
`r trend$label[peak]`. All 69,120 road-frame values are present. The observations
cover the supplied segment selection, not all city roads. The unknown physical
unit prevents a direct magnitude comparison with Beijing or PeMS hourly rates.
No event table is supplied. The daily curve preserves `meanVolume`, which the
source builder rounded to two decimal places. Selected-interval statistics above
are calculated from the saved road arrays and can differ slightly from this
rounded series.

## Saved congestion and source summaries

```{r saved-metric-inventory}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Metric=c("Volume","Speed","Congestion index"),
  Field=c("volume","speed","congestion"),
  Values=c(length(x$values),length(x$metrics$speed),length(x$metrics$congestion)),
  Unit=c(x$unit,x$metric_info$speed$unit,x$metric_info$congestion$unit),
  Saved_series=c("meanVolume","meanSpeed","congestionMean")),
  caption="Retained source measurements and frame summaries")
```

```{r congestion-map, fig.cap="Saved congestion index at the same selected interval, using the supplied source gradient."}
plot(x,index=index,metric="congestion")
```

```{r congestion-statistics}
congestion_summary <- traffic_summary(x,index=index,metric="congestion")
knitr::kable(congestion_summary[c("available","missing","zero","minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=3,caption="Selected-interval saved congestion index")
```

```{r congestion-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Source congestionMean series, retained at its saved precision."}
congestion_trend <- traffic_trend(x,metric="congestion",method="provided")
plot(congestion_trend,index=index)
```

`congestionMean` is the saved mean over all 720 segments, rounded to three
decimal places by the source builder. `meanSpeed` is also retained: it averages
speed only over segments with positive volume, so it is not a mean over every
road. The speed array remains available to statistics and explicit metric
selection; no speed display scale is supplied. A duration figure is absent
because the source supplies neither duration records nor a duration rule.

## Figure and data export

`traffic_export()` writes maps, trend figures and the selected data and summary tables for the same input and interval.

```{r export}
if(params$export) {
  label <- gsub("[^[:alnum:]_-]+","-",x$time_labels[index])
  traffic_export(x,file.path(params$export_dir,label),index=index,
    input_files=c(source="data/source.rds",prepared="data/input.rds"),trend_method="provided")
  traffic_export(x,file.path(params$export_dir,paste0(label,"-congestion")),index=index,
    metric="congestion",trend_method="provided",
    input_files=c(source="data/source.rds",prepared="data/input.rds"))
}
```
